#Sensitivity analyses for planned mulilevel models (now primary analysis instead of simple reg)

```{r cars}
 
#Sensitivity analysis under plausible assumptions  

# With MLM power, you normally need:
# ICC, residual variance, random-effects structure, cluster sizes
#b/c do not have, make and report assumptions based on prior literature:
# 
# | Quantity           | Assumption                         |
# | ------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
# | ICC (outcome)      | 0.20–0.40 (often ~0.30)            |
# | Random intercepts  | Yes                                |
# | Random slopes      | No (unless theoretically required) |
# | Level-1 predictors | Grand-mean centered                |
# | Residual SD        | 1 (standardized outcome)           |

#install.packages("lme4")
#install.packages("simr") 
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(simr)

#H1: baseline and task FAA and empathic responding 

#since Outcome variance, effect sizes of IVs, and ICC (intra-class correlation, i.e., correlation of repeated measures within participant) not yet known, using value assumptions (suggested by ChatGPT)

# Assumptions
N <- 53 #106          # number of dyads that we have eeg data for (prior to decision on which files are unusable) - NEEDS TO BE POST DATA FILE EXCLUSION
m <- 2            # number of participants per dyad
icc <- 0.3        # assumed ICC
beta0 <- 0.0      #grand mean intercept
beta1 <- 0.20 #0.17     # assumed effect for FAA_baseline
beta2 <- 0.20 #0.08     # assumed effect for FAA_task

##old starting point for beta values came from past literature (e.g., Gutsell & Inzlicht, 2012; Tullett et al., 2012); then I think I adjusted values based on fixed sample size, but with no great intention of whether best to raise or lower. Better approach might be to set all beta values to standardized small effect size and raise in same increments from there which is what I switched to above

##better document where beta values came from

# Compute variance components
var_u <- icc       # random intercept variance based on assumed icc; between-dyad variance (dyad effect)
var_e <- 1 - icc   # within-dyad residual variance; individual listener differences

# Create synthetic dataset
#FIX FOR ALL EXPAND.GRID - generates 106 dyads with 2 people each, resulting in 212 total participants. If you only have 106 participants total, you actually have $106 / 2 = 53 dyads
dat <- expand.grid( 
  dyad = factor(1:N),
  time = 1:m
)

# Simulate level 1 predictors - individual/session level (standardized)
#FAA unique to each listener role
set.seed(123)
dat$FAA_baseline <- rnorm(nrow(dat)) #varies by ptp
dat$FAA_task     <- rnorm(nrow(dat))          

# Simulate random intercepts and residuals
u_dyad <- rnorm(N, 0, sqrt(var_u))
dat$u  <- u_dyad[dat$dyad]                # Assigns shared dyad noise
dat$e  <- rnorm(nrow(dat), 0, sqrt(var_e)) # Assigns unique session noise

# Simulate outcome Y
dat$Y <- beta0 + (beta1 * dat$FAA_baseline) + (beta2 * dat$FAA_task) + dat$u + dat$e

# Fit base model
mod_resopnsetype <- lmer(Y ~ FAA_baseline + FAA_task + (1 | dyad), data = dat)
#got an error when I listed random slope as (1 + FAA_baseline + FAA_task| dyad) so leaving as random intercept only for now

summary(mod_resopnsetype)

# Step 3: Run power simulation for one IV at a time (same results should apply for affective emp and distress)
#beta values should be same to reach desired power but doesn't seem like necessary?
powerSim(mod_resopnsetype, test=fixed("FAA_baseline", "t"), nsim=500)

powerSim(mod_resopnsetype, test=fixed("FAA_task", "t"), nsim=500)


#H2: response types and psychophysiological cost

icc <- 0.3        # assumed ICC
beta0 <- 0.0      #grand mean intercept

beta2 <- #0.20     # assumed effect for affec emp
beta3 <- #0.26     # assumed effect for distress

# Compute variance components

var_e <- 1 - icc   # residual variance

# Create synthetic dataset

# Simulate predictors (standardized)
set.seed(123)

dat$AffEmp     <- rnorm(nrow(dat))

# Simulate random intercepts
u_dyad <- rnorm(N, 0, sqrt(var_u))

mod_physio <- lmer(Y ~ CogEmp + AffEmp + Distress + (1 | dyad), data = dat)

# Simulate random intercepts
```

#Sensitivity analyses for exploratory and mediation pathways

```{r cars}

#E1


#E2

#E3

set.seed(123)

nsim <- 500

# We will track mediation from Task FAA through the 3 empathy frequencies to Y
sig_med_task_cog <- 0
sig_med_task_aff <- 0
sig_med_task_dis <- 0

base_dat <- expand.grid(
  role = c("Friend_A", "Friend_B"),
  dyad = factor(1:n_dyads)
)

# 2. Define Sensitivity Betas
# Path from Baseline FAA to Task FAA
beta_base_to_task <- 0.25 

# Paths from FAA Predictors to the Mediators (Frequencies)
# Driven by BOTH Baseline and Task
base_to_cog <- 0.15;  task_to_cog <- 0.20
base_to_aff <- 0.10;  task_to_aff <- 0.22
base_to_dis <- 0.05;  task_to_dis <- -0.15

# Paths from Mediators to Outcome Y (controlling for everything else)
b_cog <-  0.25
b_aff <-  0.20
b_dis <- -0.18

# Direct effects on Outcome Y
c_prime_baseline <- 0.10
c_prime_task     <- 0.12

cat("Running Full System FAA Mediation Power Simulation...\n")

# 3. Monte Carlo Loop
for(i in 1:nsim) {
  dat <- base_dat
  
  # Dyad random effects (shared friendship variance)
  u_dyad <- rnorm(n_dyads, 0, sqrt(0.30))
  
  # Predictor 1: Baseline FAA
  dat$FAA_baseline <- rnorm(total_n, 0, 1)
  
  # Predictor 2: Task FAA (Partially driven by Baseline)
  dat$FAA_task <- (beta_base_to_task * dat$FAA_baseline) + u_dyad[dat$dyad] + rnorm(total_n, 0, sqrt(0.70))
  
  # Mediators: Frequencies (Driven by BOTH baseline and task)
  dat$M_cognitive <- (base_to_cog * dat$FAA_baseline) + (task_to_cog * dat$FAA_task) + u_dyad[dat$dyad] + rnorm(total_n, 0, sqrt(0.70))
  dat$M_affective <- (base_to_aff * dat$FAA_baseline) + (task_to_aff * dat$FAA_task) + u_dyad[dat$dyad] + rnorm(total_n, 0, sqrt(0.70))
  dat$M_distress  <- (base_to_dis * dat$FAA_baseline) + (task_to_dis * dat$FAA_task) + u_dyad[dat$dyad] + rnorm(total_n, 0, sqrt(0.70))
  
  # Outcome Y
  dat$Y <- (c_prime_baseline * dat$FAA_baseline) + (c_prime_task * dat$FAA_task) +
           (b_cog * dat$M_cognitive) + (b_aff * dat$M_affective) + (b_dis * dat$M_distress) + 
           u_dyad[dat$dyad] + rnorm(total_n, 0, sqrt(0.70))
  
  # 4. Fit the Full Stepwise Models
  # Step 1: Predict Mediators using BOTH Baseline and Task FAA
  m_cog <- lmer(M_cognitive ~ FAA_baseline + FAA_task + (1|dyad), data = dat)
  m_aff <- lmer(M_affective ~ FAA_baseline + FAA_task + (1|dyad), data = dat)
  m_dis <- lmer(M_distress  ~ FAA_baseline + FAA_task + (1|dyad), data = dat)
  
  # Step 2: Predict Y using everything simultaneously
  m_y <- lmer(Y ~ FAA_baseline + FAA_task + M_cognitive + M_affective + M_distress + (1|dyad), data = dat)
  
  # 5. Extract P-values specifically for the Task FAA -> Frequencies -> Y pathways
  p_task_to_cog <- summary(m_cog)$coefficients["FAA_task", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  p_task_to_aff <- summary(m_aff)$coefficients["FAA_task", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  p_task_to_dis <- summary(m_dis)$coefficients["FAA_task", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  
  p_cog_to_y <- summary(m_y)$coefficients["M_cognitive", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  p_b_aff_to_y <- summary(m_y)$coefficients["M_affective", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  p_b_dis_to_y <- summary(m_y)$coefficients["M_distress", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  
  # 6. Joint Significance Check
  if(p_task_to_cog < 0.05 && p_cog_to_y < 0.05)   sig_med_task_cog <- sig_med_task_cog + 1
  if(p_task_to_aff < 0.05 && p_b_aff_to_y < 0.05) sig_med_task_aff <- sig_med_task_aff + 1
  if(p_task_to_dis < 0.05 && p_b_dis_to_y < 0.05) sig_med_task_dis <- sig_med_task_dis + 1
}

# 7. Print Power Results
cat("\n==================================================\n")
cat("FULL SYSTEM MEDIATION POWER (FROM TASK FAA)\n")
cat("==================================================\n")
cat("Power for Task FAA -> Cognitive Freq -> Y:", (sig_med_task_cog / nsim)*100, "%\n")
cat("Power for Task FAA -> Affective Freq -> Y:", (sig_med_task_aff / nsim)*100, "%\n")
cat("Power for Task FAA -> Distress Freq -> Y:",  (sig_med_task_dis / nsim)*100, "%\n")

#E5

#E6

#E7
```
